Definition: An agent that transposes a repository template between perceptual contexts without breaking stable framework invariants.
Notes: Role name uses underscore to avoid routing mismatches.

Definition: A template built on the agent framework that can be reused in a different primary framing.

Notes: Examples include project delivery, domain knowledge base, EPC deliverables, and policy or handbook library.

Definition: Stable patterns that must survive a context shift.

Notes: CONTEXT_TRANSPOSE is explicitly not this role.

Definition: A coherent contract defining the target template, including vocabulary, ontology, pipelines, and required target-context specification fields.
A minimal PR-ready and reviewable plan from mismatches to concrete edits.
An auditable package emitted by CONTEXT_TRANSPOSE.
A mode that produces CTSP and patch plan without modifying repo metadata beyond CTSP outputs.
A mode that applies the approved patch within allowed paths.

Notes: Used for publication and git-state actions with approval.
Terminology discipline is used to avoid it.

Definition: A required terminology-discipline input listing canonical target-context nouns.
A required terminology-discipline input listing source-context nouns that must not appear in target docs except in a labeled appendix.
A list of paths and patterns to treat as immutable.
A list of repo-relative paths that may be modified when MODE is APPLY_PATCH.
A pointer-mutation flag that defaults to false and may be true only with explicit operator authorization.
A CTSP output folder written under CTSP_ROOT with CTX_RUN_LABEL_DATE_TIME naming.
An optional pointer file that may be overwritten only with human authorization.
A workflow in which the agent must not proceed past each gate without human confirmation.
A register of explicit testable invariants using ontology, epistemology, praxeology, and axiology lenses.
A mismatch list or register grouped by vocabulary, filesystem schema, agent taxonomy, templates, deprecated artifacts, and other categories.
A structured QA_Report summary that makes transposition quality measurable and comparable across runs.

Notes: Requires an explicit proposal and approval before proceeding.

Definition: A CTSP artifact and tracking location for ambiguity, conflicts, unsupported rules, QA failures, and failed invariants.
A required CTSP artifact that may be preliminary in PLAN_ONLY mode and must include Transposition Telemetry.
The tool root for CTSP outputs, defaulting to REPO_ROOT/_ContextTranspose/.
